key_insight: A stacking machine-learning model using pre-operative clinical features predicted which Mohs surgery cases would require 13 or more tissue sections with strong accuracy.
clinical_relevance: If validated externally, this tool could help clinicians plan operating time, allocate resources, and counsel patients before Mohs micrographic surgery.
method: 408 consecutive Mohs procedures were analyzed with 16 pre-operative clinical variables.
Thirty models were tested, including ensemble methods, gradient boosting, neural networks, SVMs, and traditional classifiers.
Performance was evaluated with 5-fold stratified cross-validation and an independent test set; SHAP was used to identify key predictors.
evidence_signal: The stacking ensemble achieved the best performance, with cross-validation AUC 0.891 and test AUC 0.884, and produced 70.7% high-confidence predictions.
watch_item: This is a single-cohort study, so external validation across centers and practice patterns is still needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting 13 or More Sections in Mohs Micrographic Surgery
